subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & rate limits (FinSecure)
messages:

Subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & rate limits (FinSecure)

Hi Samira —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discussion and the items we agreed to follow up on. Please flag anything I missed or mischaracterized.

Attendees:
- Samira Khan (FinSecure)
- Marissa Cole (Redwood)
- Vivek Kulkarni (Redwood, infra)
- Dev Patel (Redwood, solutions)

High-level goal:
FinSecure needs predictable, per-customer inference controls so you can offer tiered plans without noisy tenants impacting others. You want strong isolation (rate limits/quotas), per-customer routing/policy controls, and clear billing/usage accounting.

Pain points you described:
- Noisy tenants causing spikes and throttling for premium customers
- Current stack: multi-tenant service on GKE + OpenAI endpoints; limited per-tenant throttling in-app (custom middleware) which is brittle
- Need per-customer routing to dedicated capacity for enterprise accounts
- Lack of native per-tenant quotas and tiering (free/dev/prod) leads to manual work and billing reconciliation issues
- Need audit logs and tagging to support chargeback and compliance reviews

Success criteria (what FinSecure needs to consider this solved):
- Per-tenant rate limiting and quota enforcement (configurable by customer and by route)
- Ability to route traffic for specific tenants to different capacity pools (shared vs dedicated)
- Clear telemetry: per-tenant token counts, p95 latency, errors, and audit logs for requests
- Operational controls: per-tenant throttling policies, circuit-breakers, and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants when capacity constrained
- Latency target: p95 < 200ms for premium tenants on production traffic
- Billing accuracy: per-tenant usage exported for billing (CSV / API)

Notes on multi-tenancy controls we discussed:
- Rate limits vs quotas: you want both — short-window per-second limits to protect latency SLOs and longer-window quotas (daily/monthly) tied to plan entitlement
- Per-route policies: different endpoints (chat vs embeddings) should be independently configurable
- Tiering needs: free/dev tenants should be routed to lower-cost model variants or throttled more aggressively; paid tenants get higher throughput and reserved capacity
- Per-customer routing: policy engine should allow rules (by tenant id, tag) to route to pools labeled "shared", "dedicated-enterprise", or specific hardware/region
- Auditability: request-level metadata (tenant id, request id, model, tokens) needs to be retained for 30/90 days depending on plan (you mentioned compliance constraints)

Next steps we agreed on:
1) I’ll share a short multi-tenancy requirements worksheet (attached) so you can mark must-haves vs nice-to-haves.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra team (Vivek + Dev to run) — 60 mins to walk config examples and routing rules.
3) Provide a ballpark cost/ops estimate for Dedicated and Private options and an example rollout plan for 50–100 enterprise tenants.
4) Share SOC2 / compliance docs and sample audit log formats (if helpful).

Attachments: multi-tenancy-requirements.xlsx (worksheet to capture entitlements, retention, rate limits)

If that all looks right, can you confirm who else from FinSecure should join the technical deep-dive and a couple slots that work next week?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — this is a great recap and captures the discussion well. A few clarifications / additions from our side: 

- Success criteria: in addition to p95 latency, we need the ability to enforce different retention windows per plan (dev: 7 days, prod: 30 days, enterprise: 90 days) for both logs and request metadata.
- We need per-tenant model-tiering rules (e.g., "premium" tenants always route to the latest LLM or our pinned high-capacity model; "free" tenants route to a lower-cost variant).
- For audit/compliance: retained audit logs must be exportable (API + CSV).
- Procurement timeline: we're aiming to select a vendor by end of March with a pilot in April. Cost ballpark will be important for our procurement team.

I’ve looped in Liam (Director of Platform) to help coordinate the technical deep-dive and to validate our capacity numbers. He’ll also be the primary contact for procurement questions.

For the deep-dive, we can do:
- Tue Mar 3rd 10:00–11:00 PT or
- Wed Mar 4th 13:00–14:00 PT

Either works for us — let us know what works for your infra team.

Thanks,
Samira
Head of Product, FinSecure
samira@finsecure.com
